source_text: Ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ θυσίαις πολλαῖς καὶ πλοκαῖς ἀνθῶν τιμῶμεν, οὓς ἄνθρωποι μορφώσαντες καὶ ἐν ναοῖς ἱδρύσαντες θεοὺς προσωνόμασαν, ἐπεὶ ἄψυχα καὶ νεκρὰ ταῦτα γινώσκομεν καὶ θεοῦ μορφὴν μὴ ἔχοντα (οὐ γὰρ τοιαύτην ἡγούμεθα τὸν θεὸν ἔχειν τὴν μορφήν, ἣν φασί τινες εἰς τιμὴν μεμιμῆσθαι), ἀλλ᾿ ἐκείνων τῶν φανέντων κακῶν δαιμόνων καὶ ὀνόματα καὶ σχήματα ἔχειν. Τί γὰρ δεῖ εἰδόσιν ὑμῖν λέγειν, ἃ τὴν ὕλην οἱ τεχνῖται διατιθέασι ξέοντες καὶ τέμνοντες καὶ χωνεύοντες καὶ τύπτοντες; Καὶ ἐξ ἀτίμων πολλάκις σκευῶν διὰ τέχνης τὸ σχῆμα μόνον ἀλλάξαντες καὶ μορφοποιήσαντες θεοὺς ἐπονομάζουσιν. Ὅπερ οὐ μόνον ἄλογον ἡγούμεθα, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐφ᾿ ὕβρει τοῦ θεοῦ γίνεσθαι, ὃς ἄῤῥητον δόξαν καὶ μορφὴν ἔχων ἐπὶ φθαρτοῖς καὶ δεομένοις θεραπείας πράγμασιν ἐπονομάζεται. Καὶ ὅτι οἱ τούτων τεχνῖται ἀσελγεῖς εἰσι καὶ πᾶσαν κακίαν, ἵνα μὴ καταριθμῶμεν, ἔχουσιν, ἀκριβῶς ἐπίστασθε· καὶ τὰς ἑαυτῶν παιδίσκας συνεργαζομένας φθείρουσιν. Ὤ τῆς ἐμβροντησίας, ἀνθρώπους ἀκολάστους θεοὺς εἰς τὸ προσκυνεῖσθαι πλάσσειν λέγεσθαι καὶ μεταποιεῖν, καὶ τῶν ἱερῶν, ἔνθα ἀνατίθενται, φύλακας τοιούτους καθιστάναι, μὴ συνορῶντας ἀθέμιτον καὶ τὸ νοεῖν ἢ λέγειν ἀνθρώπους θεῶν εἶναι φύλακας.
pass_a_gloss: But neither with many sacrifices and braids of flowers do we honor those whom men, having shaped and established in temples, have named gods, since we know these things to be inanimate and dead and not having the form of God (for we do not think God has such a form as some say has been imitated in honor), but rather they have the names and shapes of those apparent evil demons. For what need is there for me to tell you things that craftsmen, shaping and cutting and hollowing and hammering, assign to the material? And from worthless things, having changed only the shape through craft and having shaped, they name them gods. Which we think is not only irrational, but also occurs due to hubris against God, who, having unspeakable glory and form, is named over perishable and needy things. And that the craftsmen of these things are shameless and have all wickedness, so as not to enumerate, you know accurately; and they corrupt their own servant girls who work together with them. Oh the shamelessness, that lawless men are said to fashion and transform into gods to be worshiped, and to establish such guards of the sacred things, where they are placed, not seeing that it is unlawful to think or to say that men are guards of gods.

rejected: to think or to speak unthinkable and unspeakable things

pass_b_english: We honor those whom men have shaped, set up in temples, and called gods neither with many sacrifices nor with braids of flowers, since we know these things are inanimate and dead and do not have the form of God. For we do not think God has such a form as some say has been imitated in honor; rather, they bear the names and shapes of those apparent evil demons. Why need I tell you what craftsmen assign to the material by shaping, cutting, hollowing, and hammering it? And from worthless things, by changing only the shape through craft and shaping it, they name them gods. We consider this not only irrational but also an act of hubris against God, who, possessing unspeakable glory and form, is named over perishable and needy things. And you know accurately that the craftsmen of these things are shameless and possess every wickedness, so as not to enumerate it; they corrupt their own servant girls who work alongside them. Oh the shamelessness, that lawless men are said to fashion and transform into gods to be worshiped, and to appoint such men as guards of the sacred places where they are set up, not seeing that it is unlawful even to think or to say that men are guards of gods.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Greek text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the complex syntax of the first sentence and the rhetorical questions. The distinction between the form of God and the form of demons is preserved. The translation of 'πλοκαῖς ἀνθῶν' as 'braids of flowers' is faithful to the Greek. The translation of 'ἀσελγεῖς' as 'shameless' and 'ὕβρει' as 'hubris' is appropriate.

Pass B: 'We honor those whom men have shaped, set up in temples, and called gods neither with many sacrifices nor with braids of flowers' misrepresents the Greek, which says 'we do not honor with many sacrifices and braids of flowers those whom men, having shaped and established in temples, have named gods.' Pass B inverts the structure, making it seem as though the Christians do honor the gods, which is incorrect. Pass B: 'they bear the names and shapes of those apparent evil demons' is missing the Greek phrase 'καὶ ὀνόματα καὶ σχήματα ἔχειν' ('and have names and shapes'), which is essential to the meaning. Pass B: 'possessing unspeakable glory and form' misrepresents the Greek 'ἐπὶ φθαρτοῖς καὶ δεομένοις θεραπείας πράγμασιν ἐπονομάζεται' ('is named over perishable and needy things'), which is a different meaning. Pass B: 'appoint such men as guards of the sacred places where they are set up' adds 'such men' which is not in the Greek, which says 'τῶν ἱερῶν, ἔνθα ἀνατίθενται, φύλακας τοιούτους καθιστάναι' ('to establish such guards of the sacred things, where they are placed')
